brief: Third in a DB CoTD series on the current Fed hiking cycle, the 15th in 70 years. Prior installments showed 10yr Treasury yields rose in the first year of 11 of the last 12 hiking cycles, and that if market pricing holds, this would be the shallowest hiking cycle in history. Today's chart (Henry Allen) plots CPI at the first hike against first-year tightening across 14 cycles, finding a tight correlation (R²=0.82): the six shallowest first-year cycles all started with CPI at or below 2%, and sub-100bps cycles started near 1% CPI. Applying DB's 3.55% CPI forecast for this month to the best-fit line implies just over 200bps of first-year hikes this cycle — an outcome DB says nobody currently expects. DB notes that ahead of the 2022 cycle markets priced only 200bps of first-year hikes versus over 400bps realized, so markets tend to underestimate hiking-cycle scale at the outset.
